tagline: Premium digital journalism and subscription-based media company
hero_kpi_rationale: The number of digital subscribers is the primary driver of revenue growth and directly reflects the success of the company's digital transformation strategy.

kpis.name: Total Subscribers
kpis.explanation: Total number of subscribers to print and digital products.
kpis.description: The total number of subscribers, including digital and print, is a key indicator of the reach and engagement of the user base.
kpis.signal: Continued growth in digital and print subscribers.

kpis.name: Digital-only Subscribers
kpis.explanation: Number of subscribers to exclusively digital products.
kpis.description: This KPI measures the traction of the digital transition strategy, a central element of the company's business model.

kpis.name: Digital-only ARPU
kpis.explanation: Average revenue generated per digital subscriber on a monthly basis.
kpis.description: Indicates the ability to monetize the digital subscriber base, potentially reflecting price increases or changes in subscription mix.
kpis.signal: Increase in revenue per digital subscriber.

kpis.name: Cash and Marketable Securities
kpis.explanation: Total amount of cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities held by the company.
kpis.description: Indicates the company's liquidity and financial flexibility for operations, investments, and shareholder returns.

kpis.name: Debt-free Status
kpis.explanation: The company has no debt on its balance sheet.
kpis.description: The absence of debt reduces financial risk and increases operational and strategic flexibility.

kpis.name: Share Repurchases
kpis.explanation: Amount of shares repurchased by the company during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Indicates the capital return policy to shareholders, complementing dividends and optimizing capital structure.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via repurchases.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.explanation: Amount of dividend paid per share (quarterly dividend approved in February 2026).
kpis.description: Reflects the company's value distribution policy to shareholders and confidence in future performance.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.description: Revenue extracted from SEC EDGAR companyfacts XBRL over the last 8 reported fiscal years (10-K).
kpis.signal: Revenue of $1.784 Bn in the latest fiscal year (FY2020).

kpis.name: DPS
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 fiscal years reported by the company.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $0.41 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $0.11 Bn in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Percentage of net income distributed as dividends: 32.1% in the latest year.

kpis.name: Bundle and multiproduct subscribers
kpis.explanation: Number of digital subscribers who subscribe to bundled or multiproduct offers.
kpis.description: Indicates the cross-selling strategy and the ability to increase value per subscriber through combined and packaged offers.

risks.title: Generative AI Litigation
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly mentioned with a 23.3% increase in costs over one year, indicating escalation. The language highlights recurring and increasing costs, and the topic is new in operating expenses. The 'Litigation' category is highly critical in media.

risks.title: Pension Cost Volatility
risks.score_rationale: The risk is recurring (cited p.33-34), with explicit mention of volatility due to discount rates and returns. The amount of adjustments is increasing ($2,967M in 2025 vs -$2,980M in 2024). The size of obligations weighs on results.

risks.title: Dependence on Digital Growth
risks.score_rationale: Revenue growth relies on digital subscriptions (+14.3%), but 'news-only' subscribers declined by 27%. The risk is implicit but central: loss of relevance of the flagship product. The shift in communication on segments reinforces this concern.

risks.title: Future Multiemployer Pension Contributions
risks.score_rationale: Mention of 'additional' future obligations for multiemployer pensions (p.34), without specific amount. The risk is latent but real, especially after a negative adjustment in 2025. The 'Capital' category is medium-weighted.

risks.title: Decline in Print and 'News-only' Digital Subscribers
risks.score_rationale: Loss of 620,000 'news-only' subscribers (-27%) and 40,000 print subscribers in one year (p.36). The language is factual but the trends are structural. Direct impact on core business.

risks.title: Risk of Excessive Shareholder Payouts
risks.score_rationale: Commitment to distribute 50% of FCF, while AI and pension costs are rising. The balance sheet is healthy ($1.2B in cash), but the risk is compromising financial flexibility if revenues slow.

ai_positioning.summary: The NYT company does not mention artificial intelligence in its report. There is no significant mention of AI or machine learning in the provided text.
